own_solution.law: Q = n C_m dT with C_m = 3R (Dulong-Petit), n = m/M
assumptions: no heat loss so all heat supplied goes to the block
constant molar heat capacity 3R over 300-360 K
work of thermal expansion negligible (C_p ~ C_v ~ 3R as stated)

TA856.regime: classical equipartition regime T well above the Debye temperature (T >~ Theta_D); 300-360 K vs 105 K is inside it

T9737.regime: classical equipartition regime T >~ Theta_D; 300-360 K vs 105 K is inside it

defect_reasons.other: For TC49F, lead 'cast' onto the block suggests molten lead; the text relies on the base statement that the block is at 300 K when heating begins, which is the natural reading but leaves the added lead's temperature implicit.

notes: n = 500/207.2 = 2.4131 mol; 3R*dT = 24.942*60 = 1496.52 J/mol; Q = 3611.3 J. With 0.68 kg: n = 3.2819 mol, Q = 4911.4 J. Heater power fixes only the heating time t = Q/P, not Q; I class it C (it enters Q = P t but cancels from Q); D would also be defensible. Variant pairs checked: TA290/TC49F, TD22B/T6CF0 both state 0.18 kg; TA856/T9737 both 105 K; T30A5/TBFB5 both 310 W; T85DA/TAA2E both 'small amount'. All consistent.
